clue.text: Wild gardens-nice for young members of the family

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so the letters of the hyphenated words run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admires a nice, untamed garden as a place for the family's children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' signals an anagram of the eleven letters of GARDENS and NICE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Daughters of a person's nephew or niece are among the younger relatives in the family tree.

clue.text: Joke about reel, though out of breath

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for a joke goes round the word for reel

parts.note: a gag is a joke
to reel is to spin round dizzily

explanation.surface: A comedian tells a joke about a fishing reel while panting for air.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is panting and gulping for air is breathless.

clue.text: Collected maps of mountains?

definitions.meaning: the ... range of mountains in north-west Africa

explanation.definitionFit: A book of maps shares its name with the North African mountain range, the question mark flagging the second reading.

clue.text: Lithic result of an idler holding up pious holy man

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the idler's word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a drone is a lazy idler, like the male bee

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for pious is read from bottom to top

parts.note: PI is a crossword abbreviation for pious
ST, saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: A lazy man supports a devout saint, with some stony consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lithic' means of stone; the definition points to a deposit formed by dripping water. 'up', in a down clue, turns PI so it reads IP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone formation built up by dripping water, such as a stalactite, is a result in rock.

clue.text: A particular time should be arranged

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the four letters of the time word are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A specific moment ought to be fixed in a diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be arranged' signals an anagram of TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular is a single detail or article in a list, just as an entry on an agenda is.

clue.text: Found press unyielding

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: A foundry worker makes a press that will not give way.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal poured into moulds is rigid and brittle, so the term describes anything inflexible.

clue.text: Can get in the way, though little

indicators.note: get in means go inside, so the word can is placed within the street abbreviation

parts.note: ST, street, is a way
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something small may still obstruct you.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre or barely sufficient amounts are small in quantity.

clue.text: Frank, left inside, stares curiously around

indicators.note: inside means the letter for left is placed within the rearranged letters
curiously means in an odd way, so the letters of stares are rearranged

explanation.surface: Frank, abandoned in a room, finds people gazing at him oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curiously' rearranges STARES to ARTESS, and L goes 'inside' it; 'around' merely confirms the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guileless and without cunning is open and honest.

clue.text: Chaff is not good for those of advanced years

parts.note: bad is the opposite of good
in age suggests being advanced in years, elderly

explanation.surface: Light grain husks are said to be unhealthy for the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaff' as a verb or noun means teasing banter, not grain husks.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is light-hearted teasing, the same as playful banter.

clue.text: Itis to live when to live is torment" (Othello)

definitions.text: Itis to live when to live is torment" (Othello)

parts.words: Itis to live when to live is torment" (Othello)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Shakespeare's Othello, where Roderigo calls living in torment foolish; the missing word completes his line after It is

explanation.surface: A line from Othello with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue reads 'It is — to live when to live is torment'; the missing word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Roderigo says it is foolishness to go on living in torment.

clue.text: A bit detached

parts.note: a part is a bit of something

explanation.surface: Something slightly aloof.
explanation.definitionFit: Things separated from one another are disconnected or set aside.

clue.text: Assert sit-ins are wrong

indicators.note: wrong means not in the right order, so the letters of sit-ins are rearranged

explanation.surface: A protester claims that occupations by demonstrators are a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are wrong' signals an anagram of SITINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something firmly and demand it be accepted is to maintain it forcefully.

clue.text: Retiring assistant people harangue

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the word for assistant is read in reverse

parts.note: an aid is an assistant, as in a nurse's aid
a tribe is a people

explanation.surface: A retiring helper delivers a lecture to the people.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter, lengthy verbal attack is a tirade.

clue.text: Medico imprisoned for harmless frolic

annotationWithheld.why: Medico imprisoned for harmless frolic: MB inside GAOL, but 'imprisoned' must both supply GAOL and signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Sent back before midday to wait, appear sick ofit

indicators.note: sent back means returned, so the letters for before midday are reversed

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means before midday
to linger is to wait around

explanation.surface: Someone sent home in the morning hangs around, looking fed up with it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent back' turns AM into MA. The printed clue ends 'appear sick of it'; the held text has 'ofit' run together.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign illness to avoid work is to shirk by pretending to be poorly.

clue.text: Holds back as large animals are seen

parts.note: for can mean as, in the sense of 'taken for' or 'as' a substitute
bears are large animals

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates when big beasts appear.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain or restrain oneself is to hold back.

clue.text: Game for some music?

definitions.meaning: a table game with balls and pins
a short, light piece of music

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tabletop ball game and a short, light piano piece.

clue.text: The cowboy drove many a champion

parts.note: ran a business, or drove cattle
C is the Roman numeral 100, standing for many
a hero is a champion

explanation.surface: The cowboy drove a great number of cattle, like a champion.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher or ranch hand in the American south-west is a cattleman.

clue.text: Trifle could become dear in the latter part of the year

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters are placed inside the season word

parts.words: the latter part of the year
parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn, the later part of the year

indicators.note: could become means turn into something else, so the letters of dear are reordered

explanation.surface: A dessert might be made especially costly near the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could become' rearranges DEAR to DERA, which goes 'in' FALL, autumn in American English.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or a trivial, showy trinket is a mere bauble.

clue.text: Ship one in smooth container as it's easily split

indicators.note: in means the ship and one are placed within the smoothing tool

parts.note: a file both smooths surfaces and holds papers
SS, steamship, is a ship
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A ship sits in a box, as if it might break apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text runs 'as it's easily' together.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock or atoms that cleave or undergo fission are readily divided.

clue.text: Gave consent for the old folk to receive a note

indicators.note: receive means take in, so the word for the old folk takes in the note

parts.note: the aged are old people
re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Permission was granted for elderly people to get a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To say yes or concur is to assent.

clue.text: Justify rate

definitions.meaning: to be worthy of, as in 'rate a mention'

explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is both to warrant it and to be worthy of it.

clue.text: A few words in condemnation of the delinquent

definitions.meaning: the punishment a judge passes on an offender

explanation.definitionFit: A group of words with subject and verb, and the penalty a court imposes, share one name.

clue.text: Standing to attention before the court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
CT is an abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: Someone stands stiffly to attention in front of the judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing straight and upright is the posture of attention.

clue.text: Flowers once worn about the neck

definitions.meaning: scented garden plants of the genus Matthiola
a stiff cravat or neckcloth of former times

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both fragrant garden blooms and old-fashioned neckcloths.

clue.text: Company about to declare capital

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the company abbreviation goes round the word for declare

parts.note: to air views is to declare them

explanation.surface: A firm is about to announce its funds.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Nile is Egypt's seat of government.

clue.text: Science graduate backing a blackleg

parts.note: SC is an abbreviation for science

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the graduate's degree letters are reversed

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A science graduate supports a strike-breaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns BA into AB. A blackleg is British for a worker who breaks a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who crosses a picket line is a strikebreaker.

clue.text: She's in need of an entire new outfit

indicators.note: in means the name sits inside the run of letters across the words

explanation.surface: A woman needs a whole new set of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across entIRE NEw.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name stands for any she.

clue.text: Does better than Rio returning to make aspiring declamation

parts.note: to excel is to do better than others

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters of the word are read in reverse

parts.note: the Brazilian city Rio, whose letters the setter meant to give ROI once turned

explanation.surface: Someone outdoes a trip back from Brazil with a stirring cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' should turn the city name round, but RIO reversed is OIR; the setter needed IOR, so the printed Rio is a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin cry meaning 'ever higher' is a motto of upward ambition.

clue.text: Lose more, but may appear to be trying

indicators.note: may appear suggests the letters can show up in another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler may keep losing, which is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may appear' signals an anagram of LOSE MORE BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irksome or vexing is difficult to put up with.
